title: Light, Photosynthesis, PPFD and Daily Light Integral
summary: Plant lighting is best understood as photon quantity, timing, spectrum and spatial distribution acting on a living canopy, not simply as fixture wattage or marketing category.

sections.title: PPFD describes photon flux at a surface
sections.body: Photosynthetic photon flux density measures the rate of photosynthetically active photons arriving at a surface. It is a point measurement and can vary substantially across a canopy, so one center-room reading cannot describe the exposure of every leaf or flower site.

sections.title: DLI integrates light through time
sections.body: Daily light integral combines photon flux with photoperiod and therefore describes the daily photon dose received at a location. Two schedules can have the same instantaneous PPFD but different DLI when their photoperiods differ, or the same DLI with different temporal delivery patterns.

sections.title: Spectrum and architecture interact
sections.body: Spectrum can influence morphology and photosynthetic behavior while architecture determines where those photons are intercepted. Recent cannabis studies reinforce that spectrum effects should be interpreted with PPFD, genotype and canopy structure rather than as an independent fixture label.
